articles.title: Philips Multigroom 7000 Series Is Nearly Half Price at Amazon UK Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days
articles.summary: Amazon UK is already dropping the price on a few grooming essentials ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, and this Philips Multigroom 7000 Series is currently £51.99, down from £94.99.
body: That's a pretty substantial £43 saving on an all-in-one trimmer designed to cover pretty much everything, from your beard and hair to your nose, ears and body. It comes with 17 attachments and 26 length settings ranging from 0.5mm to 20mm, so there's plenty of room to get the exact trim you're after without needing a drawer full of different gadgets.

The Multigroom 7000 uses self-sharpening full-metal steel blades, which Philips says stay as sharp as they were on day one without needing blade oil. There's also BeardSense technology, which scans beard density 125 times per second and automatically increases power when it detects thicker or longer hair.

For more precise work, the included precision comb offers 11 length settings between 1mm and 3mm in 0.2mm increments. There's also a narrow detail trimmer for sharper lines and finer work, alongside a metal trimmer for tidying up your cheeks, chin and neck.

At £51.99, it's a decent chunk below its usual £94.99 price, although it's worth remembering that Prime Big Deal Days itself doesn't officially start until October 6. Whether this particular deal sticks around until then, or gets replaced by an even lower price, remains to be seen.

articles.title: Netflix Tried to Bring Obsession Straight to Streaming Before It Exploded in Theaters
articles.summary: Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026. The comedian-turned-horror-filmmaker talked about the early days of his record-breaking low-budget flick during a conversation on Q with…
body: Barker said an early screening almost immediately resulted in "everybody" putting in offers to distribute Obsession. Neon, Focus, A24, and more wanted to bring Barker's twisted monkey's paw tale under their banner. Focus eventually won the war, but not before Netflix offered to throw a wrench into things.

"All of these companies are wanting to do your movie," Barker recalled hearing from his manager. "At this time, I'm still thinking maybe small theatrical release. Maybe they just want to acquire it, and also, as a director, I'm thinking, I'm scared of, 'Are they going to want to change my movie? Are they going to want to take out certain parts that I like?'
"So many questions were being thrown around. I think Netflix was in the conversation at one point. They put in an offer to just put it straight on Netflix. All of these conversations started."

articles.title: 13 Years Ago, One Dark JRPG Proved Atlus Could Still Be Hardcore
articles.summary: Today, we recognize Atlus for the Persona, Etrian Odyssey, and Trauma Center franchises, as well as for the years it spent publishing interesting RPGs from smaller Japanese developers that otherwise might never have made it to North America. That history is worthwhile.
body: Released on May 23, 2013, in Japan and brought west two months later, Shin Megami Tensei 4 was the follow-up fans had been craving for the better part of a decade. Instead of visits to hot springs and the beach, players navigated the hellscape that once had been Tokyo. They roamed foreboding corridors populated by demons out for blood, recruiting some of them while facing the possible extinction of humanity itself.

As later proved by 2021’s Shin Megami Tensei 5, Atlus has managed to keep both the Shin Megami Tensei and Persona franchises going strong. But Shin Megami Tensei 4 launched when that future was in doubt, and it did so on the last piece of hardware you might expect: the Nintendo 3DS. The game was dark and brutal, just like Nocturne. It launched with a CD full of eerie musical selections, as well as a 176-page “Strategy & Design Book” produced with strategy publisher Prima Games.

articles.title: Don't Breathe 3 in the Works With Stephen Lang and Jane Levy, Fede Álvarez Says
articles.summary: Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles. The filmmaker behind some of the grislier horror movies of the last 15 years announced his intentions to finish his thriller trilogy with a proper third…
body: How the third Don't Breathe movie will materialize and what story it will tell remains unclear. However, it sounds like it will at least continue where the previous two films left off, with both Stephen Lang (Avatar) and Jane Levy (Evil Dead) expected to reprise their roles as The Blind Man a.k.a. Norman Nordstrom and Rocky, respectively.

Álvarez and Levy previously worked together on his 2013 Evil Dead reboot before re-teaming for the original Don't Breathe in 2016. The horror-thriller, which was also produced by scary movie visionary Sam Raimi, follows three thieves who break into a house before finding themselves fighting for their lives in a "lethal game of cat and mouse."

Don't Breathe 2 continued the story with Lang back as The Blind Man in 2021. The sequel saw Álvarez hand directing duties to frequent collaborator Rodo Sayagues, with Raimi also returning as producer. In the five years since its premiere, there have been few updates about how the crew might round out the trilogy with a Don't Breathe 3 despite Lang teasing a new movie through the years.

articles.title: 'Forgotten Island's Stars Explain "Tayo Na!", the Movie's Biggest Shifting In-Joke
articles.summary: In the new DreamWorks animated movie Forgotten Island, the two teenage leads, Jo and Raissa, say the same phrase to each other over and over: “Tayo na!” As with a lot of the other Filipino cultural elements in the movie, writer-directors Joel Crawford and Januel P.
body: But that can be a little difficult when the context changes from scene to scene — and when the phrase itself has a variety of meanings. As Filipinos and Tagalog speakers have been explaining online, “Tayo na!” can colloquially mean “Let’s go!” or “You and me!” or “Get up!” depending on pronunciation, who’s speaking, and whether there’s a romantic, parental, or other context.

Forgotten Island uses the phrase in a lot of different ways as Jo and Raissa, two childhood friends confronting hidden tensions and big changes in their relationship, either urge each other into adventure or rev each other up in the face of danger. The first time Jo says it, when she first meets Raissa, she actually says, "Let's go! Tayo na!" It seems very casual at first, but throughout the movie, it takes on new weight and bigger meanings.
The characters’ voice actors, Liza Soberano (Raissa) and singer-songwriter H.E.R. (Jo), tell Polygon that their own Filipino roots played into how they interpreted the phrase from scene to scene.

articles.title: Control Resonant's Completely Ignores The Most Interesting Character
articles.summary: As a sequel to 2019’s Control, Control Resonant makes an effort to stand on its own. The lockdown in the Oldest House is over, and Dylan Faden is charged with saving the world (a.k.a. Manhattan), which is now suffering the effects of both the Hiss and a new paranormal entity.
body: The Oldest House is an entity in itself. Within Remedy's universe, it is called a "place of power," which means that paranatural forces have affected it. From the outside, it looks like a regular government building. The brutalist architecture, the somber tones, and its imposing height make it weird, but, you know, a government-owned kind of weird. But the Oldest House is more than meets the eye.

First, it existed before becoming the Federal Bureau of Control's headquarters. Instead of being built or rented, the place was found. Second, the Oldest House is only visible to those who are looking for it, which means that one must first conceive its existence for it to actually materialize in the reality they exist in. The Oldest House is alive and connected to other dimensions. Its corridors may become interdimensional mazes, and its doors may lead people to other parts of the planet, challenging anyone's understanding of reality.

articles.title: Xbox is reportedly paying a "fraction" of the $400 million Kojima quoted Sony for Physint
articles.summary: A reported $400 million budget for Hideo Kojima 's Physint has already been walked back over the weekend, with multiple outlets now saying Xbox is paying nowhere near that figure for Hideo Kojima's stealth game.
body: The number originated from Christopher Dring of The Game Business, who said on his podcast on Friday that Xbox was "signing Kojima for a project often referred to as Physint with a budget around $400 million".

Later, however, Dring himself clarified on X/Twitter that Xbox is likely paying "quite a bit less" than the figure Kojima had originally quoted Sony - Dring originally said he'd heard "everything from $300 million to $600 million, although it's $400 million that is the figure that is bandied around" - and Bloomberg's Jason Schreier said his own sources described Microsoft's negotiated figure as "significantly less than this".
Windows Central's Jez Corden went further, saying Xbox is paying only a "fraction" of it, although neither source reported an actual figure.

Physint, Kojima Productions' action-espionage title and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, was originally announced as a PlayStation project. Sony reportedly spent months negotiating with the studio before pulling its funding after the project exceeded budget and missed deadlines.

articles.title: Witcher Dev Reveals Why CD Projekt Red Doesn't Do Crossovers In Its Own Games
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red's The Witcher and Cyberpunk franchises are no stranger to collaborations and crossover with other games. At BlizzCon, we learned that a Geralt-inspired Barbarian skin is coming to Diablo 4 and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners outfits are headed to Overwatch next year.
body: I asked CD Projekt Red why this was the case at BlizzCon earlier this month. Level design lead Miles Tost explained that the lack of crossover or collaboration content in CD Projekt Red's own games comes down to the studio wanting content parity across all platforms. CD Projekt Red is open to changing that approach in the future, though.

When asked directly whether CD Projekt Red had considered putting Diablo-themed content in The Witcher games, Tost admitted that "we haven't really thought about this yet." He added that CD Projekt Red has historically preferred physical goodies as platform-exclusive bonuses rather than any sort of exclusive content.

"One thing we really value is to not have content that is purely exclusive depending on where you buy," he said. "Usually, when we need to do something exclusive for [partners], what we've done in the past are things like an exclusive physical hoodie. I can recall we did this for Xbox. Xbox pre-orders for The Witcher 3 got an exclusive set of cards. For us, it's really important to preserve that, if you buy the game and play it, you always get the full version of it."

articles.title: Gears of War story director laid off mere days after E-Day went gold
articles.summary: Gears of War: E-Day is almost here, but that doesn't mean its developers have been spared in Microsoft's latest wave of layoffs as part of the Xbox "reset." While The Coalition, the studio currently working on the Gears of War series, was not mentioned by name in Matt Booty's "Continuing Our Reset"…
body: "I am part of this round of Microsoft layoffs and am open to new opportunities in games/film/tv," he wrote. "If your team needs a director/storyteller please reach out." It is perhaps especially galling given that Gears of War: E-Day went gold just days before the layoffs were announced, with a full release planned for Oct. 6.

It has felt increasingly like there is simply no amount of success, sales, acclaim, or back-breaking work you can demonstrate in the games industry to avoid some pencil pusher's job cut scythe. It's not just Microsoft's massive rounds of layoffs—take a studio like Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor, which furloughed most of its staff despite glowing reviews and over a million copies sold. This situation with Vaca echoes when, last year, a writer on Apex Legends was laid off just one day after a character she spent a year writing was unveiled.

For a primer on all the most reliable ways you can get laid off in the games industry, check out our guide on that very phenomenon. It is a sobering time to wish you could cheer on the medium's every step forward, given that the reward for doing the work seems to be a kick out the door.

articles.title: I'm loving WoW: Forever, but I can't help but miss the music of my other beloved MMO
articles.summary: Uh-oh. The MMO no-life virus started coursing through me as soon as I jumped into WoW: Forever's beta, and it's refusing to let up. Which is a problem, considering I'm also housing the kind of sickness that makes me pump dozens of hours into Final Fantasy 14 every week like it's a goddamn full-time…
body: Welcome to Critical Hit, where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.

My only prior experience with Blizzard's MMO is a level 13 Paladin I made a poor attempt at trying out around the release of Battle for Azeroth nearly a decade ago. This time it's sticking. I am absolutely loving WoW: Forever's stripped-back, old-school feel, complete with sprinklings of modernity that make it palatable for folks like me who lack those rose-tinted glasses.

The one thing I'm struggling to come around to, though? The music. Not that I think it's bad. The opposite, in fact—I've been loving the ominous tones of Durotar's overworld music, and venturing into Orgrimmar for the first time I was met with the perfect grand, foreboding sound that a city for the Horde deserves.

articles.title: Five Nights at Freddy's is coming to Fortnite for Fortnitemares
articles.summary: Epic has confirmed that Five Nights at Freddy's is joining Fortnite for this year's Fortnitemares event.
body: After months of rumours and teasing, a new trailer formally confirms that Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria will appear as a location on the map, with Freddy, Bonnie, Chica and Foxy all featuring as bosses that players can take on in a fight.
"It's almost showtime!" Epic announced. "The Fazbear Band has taken over Battle Royale. Face the animatronic animal bosses and survive the night… if you can. Fortnitemares begins 1st October!"

The crossover had been expected for a while, with the pizzeria itself appearing on the island during Fortnite's Override season, and recent Fortnitemares hinting at security cameras and FNAF dialogue.

Over the summer, Epic Games settled a court case against a contractor accused of leaking Fortnite information. Former contractor Hayden Cohen agreed to a judgment that bars them from "possessing, accessing, using, or disclosing any of Epic's confidential or trade secret information", including a ban on providing confidential information to other third parties, too.

articles.title: Shadow the Hedgehog is supposed to be dead
articles.summary: It's hard to imagine Sonic the Hedgehog without his Jungian counterpart: the gun-toting, swear-uttering Shadow the Hedgehog. But Shadow is a relatively late addition to the series' extensive roster of anthropomorphic animals, debuting long after the Genesis days in Sonic Adventure 2—more than that…
body: According to a report from One More Game, Sonic honcho Takashi Iizuka said at the recent Tokyo Game Show that Shadow's popularity was a big surprise to Sonic Team when SA2 came out. "If you have played Sonic Adventure 2, people may know that Shadow basically sort of died at the end of that game," he said.

"We were originally intending to just kind of 'die the character out' (kill him off), but the character Shadow was just so very popular that we decided to revive him in Sonic Heroes.“ He also noted that Shadow is his personal favorite character, and he wants to give him more of a spotlight in the future.

Not that Shadow has ever gone completely by the wayside. He's one of the only Sonic characters other than, well, Sonic, to have his own videogame (even if it wasn't exactly acclaimed) and he was more recently the star of Sonic X Shadow Generations, the best version of one of the best Sonic games on PC. He also remains a fan-favorite among modders, who have the cure if you thought Sonic Mania ought to have been Shadow Mania. We would also be remiss if we didn't mention that the great Keanu Reeves went on a personal journey to voice the beloved bad boy erinaceid.

articles.title: Latest Xbox layoffs reportedly devastated Age of Empires developer and canceled its next game
articles.summary: The latest stage of Xbox's delicately named " reset " arrived last Tuesday —but its impact on World's Edge Studio, the developer now behind the Age of Empires series, was only briefly mentioned in Xbox CCO Matt Booty's announcement.
body: "What a morning," said former World's Edge creative director Adam Isgreen on resetera, posting under the verified account name Tempus Chaoti. "FYI World's Edge was not spared completely—just under half the studio was let go—myself included. Been fun, y'all!" This is in addition to the studio now answering to Activision alongside Sea of Thieves developer Rare.

Andrew Martz, former senior software engineer at World's Edge, posted on LinkedIn adding that "as part of that reorg, our next project was canceled and a large chunk of our studio was laid off. I was part of that layoff."

Isgreen also had more to say on LinkedIn, reflecting on his time working on the RTS series: "I didn't think I'd be working on RTS games again years after their first 'heyday,' but am I ever proud of what our studio team and partners were able to do with the series and juice the genre's return. I think the fans would agree (mostly!) that we delivered the goods for all of 'em."

articles.title: Minecraft is getting its first new dimension in 14 years, and it's called The Sift
articles.summary: Minecraft maker Mojang has announced The Sift, a new Minecraft dimension that will join the Overworld, the Nether, and The End when it launches on Java and Bedrock in 2027. It's the first new dimension added to the game since The End arrived in 2011.
body: The Sift will appear first in Minecraft Dungeons 2, slated for release on 29th September, before coming to the base game next year.

The Sift was announced during Minecraft Live on 26th September, alongside the wider Dungeons 2 reveal. We didn't get much information about it - Mojang is holding back most of the details for now - but did describe it as a new environment that will bring new biomes, mobs, and ways to play and explore. As yet, there's no firm release date.
"Minecraft Live revealed that the newest Minecraft dimension isn't just finding its home in Dungeons 2, it'll also be coming to Minecraft Java & Bedrock Edition next year," the team teased.

"This will be the first new dimension in over 14 years - joining the Overworld, the Nether and the End as our fourth dimension. During the broadcast, you got a glimpse into this dimension in Minecraft - and even one of the mobs that calls it home. But surely that's not enough! Luckily you can experience it for yourself in Minecraft Dungeons 2 - coming September 29, 2026."

Werwulf see's Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe, and Lily-Rose Depp returning from their work together on Eggers last movie; Nosferatu, for an all new terrifying take on the classic mythos.
Werwulf comes to cinemas on December 25th 2026!
